passages.title: Leave of Absence Policy
passages.text:
Full-time and part-time employees with at least 6 months of service are eligible for parental leave. It is available to any parent, for the birth of a child, an adoption or a foster placement. Interns and contractors are not eligible.
Service is counted from your hire date to the first day of your leave. Both parents may take parental leave if both work at Ridgeline. If you will reach 6 months of service shortly after the birth or placement, contact HR to discuss timing.

passages.title: Benefits Summary & Eligibility
passages.text:
During paid leave, such as paid parental leave, your benefits continue on the same terms and your contributions continue through payroll. If you take unpaid leave of more than 30 days, contact HR before the leave starts to arrange how your contributions will be paid.
Shorter unpaid leave doesn't change your benefits. When you return from any leave, your benefits continue as before; you don't need to re-enrol. Ask HR how a specific leave affects your 401(k) contributions, since contributions are based on pay received.

passages.title: Leave of Absence Policy
passages.section_heading: Benefits and PTO during parental leave
passages.text:
Your benefits continue on the same terms during parental leave, and your employee contributions continue through payroll (see also RSE-BEN-01 §4). Your PTO keeps accruing while you are on paid parental leave (RSE-PTO-01 §2.5). If your leave spans December 31, you can carry over more unused PTO than usual; see RSE-PTO-01 §5.2.
If you want to add a new child to your benefits, do it within the qualifying life event window in RSE-BEN-01 §3.4. Your HR record, Employment Type and Work Arrangement stay the same during parental leave, and you return to the same role or a similar one.

passages.title: Leave of Absence Policy
passages.text:
For employees of the Toronto office, HR coordinates Ridgeline's parental leave with the employee's government parental benefits. Plan details are available from HR.
Contact HR as early as you can, because government benefits have their own application steps and timing. HR explains how Ridgeline's paid leave and government benefits fit together for your dates; it doesn't give personal advice on government programmes.

passages.title: Leave of Absence Policy
passages.text:
Parental leave must be taken within 12 months of the birth, adoption or placement. You can take it in one continuous block, or in two blocks of at least 4 weeks each. Agree the dates with HR and let your manager know the plan.
For example, you could take 8 weeks after a birth and the remaining 4 weeks later in the year. Leave not taken within the 12 months lapses and is not paid out.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
PTO keeps accruing while you are on paid leave, such as paid parental leave. PTO does not accrue during unpaid leave, such as unpaid personal leave (RSE-LV-01 §6).
PTO accrued before and during paid leave stays in your balance, and you can use it when you return or add it to the end of your leave with the usual approval. If your leave crosses the end of the year, see §5.2 for the higher carryover cap.

passages.title: Leave of Absence Policy
passages.text:
Eligible employees get 12 weeks of paid parental leave at 100% of base pay. HR approves parental leave, and your manager is notified.
The 12 weeks are calendar weeks, so company holidays inside your leave don't extend it. Parental leave is paid through normal payroll on your usual pay dates. You can add PTO before or after your parental leave in the usual way.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
If you are on approved leave that spans December 31, you can carry over up to 10 unused PTO days instead of 5.
This applies to approved leave under the Leave of Absence Policy, such as parental leave, that is in progress on December 31. It is applied automatically when your leave is recorded in the HR Portal; you don't need to request it.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
PTO accrues each semi-monthly pay period, 24 periods a year. Each period you earn your annual days divided by 24. You can use PTO as soon as it has accrued.
This means your balance grows steadily through the year rather than arriving all at once on January 1. A new employee can take PTO early in their employment, but only the days already accrued; plan longer breaks for later in the year, when more PTO is available. Your available balance in the HR Portal already allows for days that are pending approval.

passages.title: Benefits Summary & Eligibility
passages.text:
Certain life events let you change your benefits outside open enrollment: the birth or adoption of a child, marriage, and loss of other coverage. Make the change in the HR Portal within 31 days of the event; for example, add a new baby within 31 days of the birth.
The change you make must be consistent with the event: a marriage lets you add your spouse, and the birth of a child lets you add the child and change your coverage level. HR may ask for documents that confirm the event. Changes take effect from the date of the event where the plan allows.
